findings.summary: Theme is fixed rather than following the system color preference.
findings.evidence: The rendered DOM always has the class dark; the light-preference probe reports colorScheme normal, while dark and default screenshots are visually identical.
findings.suggestedFix: Declare color-scheme: light dark and derive tokens with prefers-color-scheme or light-dark(), retaining an explicit user override.

findings.summary: Animations continue when reduced motion is requested.
findings.evidence: Under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce, eight animations remain running with 2000 ms durations and the loaded CSS exposes no reduced-motion rule.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a reduced-motion media query that removes non-essential motion and stops auto-advancing previews.

findings.summary: Route and state changes do not use View Transitions.
findings.evidence: The live CSS probe found no view-transition rules or API styling across the MPA navigation surfaces.
findings.suggestedFix: Add cross-document View Transitions for same-origin browse and detail navigation, with reduced-motion fallback.

findings.summary: Navigation chrome does not react to scroll position.
findings.evidence: The CSS probe found no scroll timeline or scroll-state implementation; the dense two-row header remains the dominant navigation treatment.
findings.suggestedFix: Use scroll-state container queries or a lightweight shrinking header so content gains space while orientation remains visible.

findings.summary: A consent modal obscures the primary content on every tested content route.
findings.evidence: Desktop screenshots for home, categories, search and video detail show the same large centered cookie overlay covering the core content. Refuse is available but content is blocked until a choice.
findings.suggestedFix: Use a compact, non-blocking consent surface where legally possible, preserve equal accept/refuse choices, and avoid repeating it across fresh navigations.

findings.summary: The blocking consent surface is implemented as custom generic containers rather than a semantic dialog.
findings.evidence: DOM and screenshot evidence show a custom overlay; the landmark probe does not expose a dialog role or dialog element for the blocking surface.
findings.suggestedFix: Use dialog/showModal with an accessible name, focus containment, Escape handling and explicit equal-choice actions.

findings.summary: Persistent chrome crowds the content.
findings.evidence: The first viewport contains two global navigation rows, a full-width age banner, a permanent category sidebar and a blocking consent modal before the video grid.
findings.suggestedFix: Collapse secondary navigation and filters progressively, reduce persistent banners, and let the media grid own the viewport.

findings.summary: The desktop layout is forced into a 360 px viewport.
findings.evidence: Layout evidence reports scrollWidth 1024 versus visualViewportWidth 360, with 664 px overflow. The mobile screenshot shows clipped header, sidebar and cards.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove desktop minimum widths, use intrinsic grid sizing and responsive navigation, and validate at 320 to 412 px without horizontal scrolling.

findings.summary: Reusable content and navigation components do not adapt at container level.
findings.evidence: The CSS probe found no @container rules while the same sidebar and card layout remains desktop-sized in the narrow capture.
findings.suggestedFix: Give reusable cards, navigation and filter regions containment and adapt them with size container queries.

findings.summary: Keyboard focus and target sizing are inadequate.
findings.evidence: The focus probe shows focused buttons with outline none and zero width; Lighthouse fails target-size, and the live probe found 30 of the first 200 visible targets below 24 px.
findings.suggestedFix: Provide a strong :focus-visible treatment and enlarge or space interactive targets to at least 24 by 24 CSS px, preferably 44 px for primary touch actions.

findings.summary: The signup journey renders an apparently empty form card.
findings.evidence: The signup screenshot shows only the card frame and headings, with the registration choices absent from the visible card although body text contains them. A user cannot identify or complete the next signup step.
findings.suggestedFix: Fix the signup card visibility/rendering state, keep each registration option visible without relying on delayed styling, and test the full guest signup flow.

findings.summary: Mobile LCP is just outside the good threshold.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse reports LCP 2.6 s; the good Core Web Vitals threshold is 2.5 s. CLS is 0 and TBT is 0 ms in that run.
findings.suggestedFix: Prioritize the actual LCP asset and critical styles, and defer non-critical account, ad and recommendation code.

findings.summary: The initial page uses a large and fragmented dependency set.
findings.evidence: The HAR records 143 requests, 61 scripts and 1,766,838 transferred bytes. One index script is 400,248 bytes and several parser-inserted styles are VeryHigh priority.
findings.suggestedFix: Reduce critical CSS and script chains, split by immediate user need, and defer recommendation, identity and advertising dependencies until required.

findings.summary: Unused CSS and JavaScript are shipped on the initial route.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse estimates 56 KiB unused CSS, including sheets 89 to 95 percent unused, and 26 KiB unused JavaScript.
findings.suggestedFix: Route-split CSS and JavaScript and conditionally load optional widgets after consent or interaction.

findings.summary: Controls and media links have incorrect or missing accessible names.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse fails button-name and label-content-name-mismatch. It identifies an unnamed 40 by 24 button and thumbnail links whose visible duration is not included in the accessible name.
findings.suggestedFix: Give every control a programmatic name that contains its visible label, and keep thumbnail title and duration relationships available to assistive technology.

findings.summary: Important banner text fails WCAG contrast.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse reports age-banner contrast ratios of 2.15:1 and 1.75:1 where 4.5:1 is required, plus links distinguishable only by low-contrast color.
findings.suggestedFix: Adjust banner and link tokens to meet 4.5:1 for normal text and add a non-color link affordance.

findings.summary: Focus visibility and list semantics are broken.
findings.evidence: The focus probe repeatedly reports outline none. Lighthouse also reports a ul with direct div, complementary and button-role children rather than list items.
findings.suggestedFix: Restore visible focus indicators and keep only li children in lists; move ads and complementary blocks outside or wrap them semantically.

findings.summary: Zoom, reflow and touch target support fail.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse detects user-scalable=no in the effective viewport and fails target-size. The 360 px layout has 664 px overflow.
findings.suggestedFix: Never disable user zoom, reflow the desktop shell for narrow widths, and increase target spacing.

findings.summary: Many image elements lack stable dimensions or are oversized.
findings.evidence: The images primitive reports 29 of 36 images without width/height and 13 oversized images; eight below-fold images are not lazy-loaded.
findings.suggestedFix: Reserve image space with width/height or aspect-ratio, tune srcset sizes to rendered slots, and lazy-load below-fold media.

findings.summary: Localized pages omit hreflang relationships.
findings.evidence: The French document has a canonical URL but the head probe found zero hreflang links despite the navigation exposing more than 40 language hosts.
findings.suggestedFix: Publish reciprocal hreflang links, including x-default where appropriate, and keep canonical, sitemap and locale-host policies consistent.

findings.summary: Rich media pages omit structured and social metadata.
findings.evidence: The homepage head probe found no JSON-LD and no Open Graph tags. The representative video detail is a rich VideoObject candidate with descriptive visible metadata.
findings.suggestedFix: Add accurate VideoObject JSON-LD on detail pages and Open Graph/Twitter preview metadata matching visible title, thumbnail and canonical URL.

findings.summary: Security headers and cookie attributes are incomplete.
findings.evidence: HTTPS and HSTS are present, but CSP is only frame-ancestors self, X-Content-Type-Options and response Referrer-Policy are missing, and two first-party cookies lack Secure; settings also uses SameSite=None.
findings.suggestedFix: Deploy a nonce or hash based CSP beyond frame-ancestors, add nosniff and a privacy-preserving Referrer-Policy, and mark all HTTPS cookies Secure with the narrowest SameSite policy.

findings.summary: The initial load has a broad third-party and tracking footprint.
findings.evidence: The tracker probe sees 15 third-party origins including Google Tag Manager. HAR attributes 116 of 143 requests and 1,654,762 of 1,766,838 bytes to origins classified as third party.
findings.suggestedFix: Gate non-essential third parties behind refusal-respecting consent, consolidate first-party CDN classification, and remove or delay trackers and widgets without immediate user value.

findings.summary: Account entry does not expose phishing-resistant authentication.
findings.evidence: The signup surface advertises Google, X and email account entry, but recon and DOM evidence expose no passkey or WebAuthn route. No permission prompt fired on load.
findings.suggestedFix: Offer passkey registration and authentication alongside federated and recovery options, with sensitive actions reauthenticated.

findings.summary: Browser-enforced privacy and XSS defenses are too narrow.
findings.evidence: The CSP only restricts framing, Permissions-Policy grants client-hint features broadly, Referrer-Policy is absent at response level, and the document requests unsafe-url in markup.
findings.suggestedFix: Adopt a restrictive CSP and Permissions-Policy, set strict-origin-when-cross-origin or stricter referrer handling, and remove unsafe-url.

findings.summary: French numeric content uses English-style compact formatting.
findings.evidence: Visible French content renders values such as 803.9K vues and 2.6M vues instead of locale-aware decimal separators and compact units.
findings.suggestedFix: Format counts with Intl.NumberFormat using the active locale and translated compact-display conventions.

findings.summary: The signup failure state provides no visible explanation or recovery.
findings.evidence: The registration card appears empty in the screenshot, but the page provides no inline error, retry action or status message explaining why signup controls are unavailable.
findings.suggestedFix: Expose loading and failure states in the card, announce errors through a live region, and provide retry or alternate sign-in actions without losing context.

findings.summary: Premium upsells do not show commitment or pricing in context.
findings.evidence: The video detail places Rejoignez maintenant and Obtenir la vidéo entière calls to action prominently, while the first viewport shows no price or commitment detail.
findings.suggestedFix: Put price, billing cadence, renewal and cancellation terms adjacent to the premium call to action before account or payment steps.

findings.summary: Media delivery wastes image bytes.
findings.evidence: The images primitive reports 13 oversized images, 16 legacy-format detections and 29 missing intrinsic dimensions among 36 images.
findings.suggestedFix: Serve correctly sized AVIF/WebP sources for each slot, retain responsive srcset, and reserve dimensions.

findings.summary: The initial route performs disproportionate script and network work.
findings.evidence: The HAR records 143 requests and 61 scripts before user interaction, including identity, tracking and recommendation dependencies; 26 KiB JS and 56 KiB CSS are estimated unused.
findings.suggestedFix: Conditionally import optional widgets, batch analytics, and postpone background recommendations until idle, consent or user intent.

findings.summary: Third-party resources dominate the transfer budget.
findings.evidence: HAR classifies 1,654,762 of 1,766,838 transferred bytes as third party, about 94 percent, across 116 requests.
findings.suggestedFix: Set a third-party budget, self-host or consolidate critical dependencies, and defer ads, identity and recommendations until they provide immediate value.

findings.summary: Repeated feed scrolling increases retained heap and graph size.
findings.evidence: After ten bottom/top scroll cycles, the heap summary rises from 36,474,321 to 39,913,095 self bytes and from 682,502 to 749,243 nodes. Separate fresh sessions make this a medium-confidence leak signal, not a proven trace.
findings.suggestedFix: Repeat the test in one controlled session with baseline, target and final snapshots; release preview, observer and lazy-load state after cards leave the interaction lifecycle.

findings.summary: The initial heap and object graph are large for a listing page.
findings.evidence: The baseline heap summary contains 682,502 nodes, 3,204,478 edges and 36,474,321 self bytes before playback.
findings.suggestedFix: Profile the largest script and native allocations, virtualize long grids, and avoid initializing optional previews and widgets before interaction.
